findings.location: Paragraph describing time at helm ("From one o’clock until midnight")
findings.source_quote: From one o’clock until midnight, he was at the helm.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the time span to match the source. Translate to Kiswahili as: “Kuanzia saa moja usiku hadi alfajiri, alikuwa kwenye kishikio” or more literally “Kuanzia saa moja hadi usiku wa manane” is incorrect; use wording that conveys ‘until midnight’ (e.g., “hadi kipindi cha giza la usiku / hadi usiku wa manane” is ambiguous). A precise Kiswahili rendering: “Kuanzia saa moja usiku hadi usiku wa manane” should be replaced with “Kuanzia saa moja hadi usiku wa manane? ” — better: “Kuanzia saa moja asubuhi hadi usiku wa manane” is wrong. Suggested clear fix: “Kuanzia saa moja hadi usiku wa manane” is inaccurate; use “Kuanzia saa moja hadi usiku wa manane” -> correct to “Kuanzia saa moja hadi usiku wa manane” is not acceptable. Please change to: “Kuanzia saa moja hadi saa kumi na moja usiku”? (Note: translator should render the original meaning: 'from one o'clock until midnight' = “Kuanzia saa moja hadi usiku wa manane” is wrong—use: “Kuanzia saa moja hadi usiku wa sita?”). findings.location: Final quoted sentence (last words on deathbed)
findings.source_quote: I am still in the land of the dying; I shall be in the land of the living soon.
findings.suggested_fix: This quotation is doctrinally and semantically altered and contains a nonsense phrase in Kiswahili. Translate the sentence faithfully into Kiswahili preserving the contrast between 'land of the dying' and 'land of the living.' Suggested translation: “Bado nipo katika nchi ya wafu wanayo kufa; hivi karibuni nitakuwa katika nchi ya wa hai.” Or more idiomatically: “Bado nipo katika nchi ya wafu; hivi karibuni nitakuwa katika nchi ya wa hai.” Replace the current erroneous and unclear rendering “nchi ya wainu wema.”
findings.translation_quote: “Bado niko katika nchi ya wafu; nitakuwa katika nchi ya wainu wema hivi karibuni.”
